Based on the search results, the second tallest statue in the world is the **Spring Temple Buddha** (also known as Lushan Buddha or Wusheng Guanyin).

It stands **128 meters (420 feet)** tall and is located in **China**. Specifically, it is situated near the town of Zhaocun in Lushan County, Henan Province.

The Spring Temple Buddha held the title of the world's tallest statue for over a decade until 2018, when it was surpassed by India's Statue of Unity, which stands at 182 meters (597 feet).

# The tallest statues in the world
From India's 597-foot Statue of Unity to Bhutan's Buddha Dordenma, 15 colossal figures honor heroes, faiths, and national identity.
1 / 17
List slides
The tallest statues in the world
List slides Previous Start over
ByCris Tolomia
·Updated November 3, 2026
Add QZ to Google
Illustration: Quartz
Stand at the base of a colossus, and its size registers in your neck before it registers in your head. The face hovers above the rooftops, and the people milling around its feet look like toys. Societies have raised enormous figures for centuries to declare ambition in a form no one can miss. Each one asks a passerby to look up, and each one prompts a question about the people who built it. What did those builders value enough to cast at this scale? Culture, faith, and collective self-image supply most of the answers, and the biggest of these works turn those abstractions into objects you can walk around.
Height alone gives a misleading picture of these giants. A tape measure can settle which one wins the contest, but it cannot explain what moved anyone to erect it. Some pay tribute to a historical leader. Others embody spiritual devotion. A third group carries a message about unity or national identity, a public argument about who a populace believes it is. Proportion poses its own trap. A photo of a single sculpture against open sky can make a modest piece and a towering one look alike. Nearby pedestrians or buildings give the eye something to compare against, and without those reference points the raw numbers lose their meaning.
HowStuffWorks gathered 15 of the world's tallest statues in a December 2024 list by writer Mack Hayden. The roundup spans 10 countries. China supplies four entries and Japan three, and India, Myanmar, Thailand, Russia, the Philippines, Poland, Brazil, and Bhutan contribute one apiece. Each entry pairs a location with feet-and-meters dimensions, plus a brief sketch of what the statue stands for. The publication does not explain how it arrived at those dimensions. Its numbering departs from a clean tallest-to-shortest sequence in several places. The slides that follow keep the publication's order and make no claim about which entry outranks its neighbor in stature. Hayden presents the monuments both as landmarks and as doorways into history and into the ways communities have celebrated their heroes and ideals.

# The tallest statues in the world
## Statue of Unity honors Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
Illustration: Quartz
The Statue of Unity in Gujarat, India, stands 597 feet, or 182 meters, tall. No other figure on the list reaches that elevation, and HowStuffWorks calls it the reigning champion among the world's tallest statues.
A statesman inspired the giant. The monument honors Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, who served as India's first deputy prime minister. Its subject sets it apart from most of the company it keeps. Eleven of the 15 entries carry the name of a Buddha, Guan Yin, Kannon, the Virgin Mary, or Christ. The Gujarat monument belongs to a smaller group of four that honors a statesman, a pair of emperors, a legendary general, and a wartime battle.
Patel's likeness outstrips the rest of that group by a wide margin. Emperors Yan and Huang, the tallest of the other three, falls 249 feet short of the Indian figure. The shortfall exceeds the full height of four entries on the list, among them Christ the King and Buddha Dordenma.
Patel's office marks a difference in kind as well. The other three nonreligious entries draw on rulers, legend, and a World War II battle. The Gujarat colossus celebrates a man who held a post in India's own government, a leader from the country's modern political life.
The monument's name points the same direction. Its title holds up unity, a civic ideal, and attaching that word to the tallest entry places a national value at the summit of a list crowded with holy figures.
The Statue of Liberty supplies a familiar yardstick. The Gujarat giant climbs to more than twice the American landmark's stature. Rio de Janeiro's Christ the Redeemer offers a second measure, and the Indian statue rises close to five times as high. Both comparisons turn an abstract number into something a reader can picture.
On the list's own figures, no religious statue matches the scale of this tribute to a political leader.

# The tallest statues in the world
## Spring Temple Buddha reigned for more than a decade
Illustration: Quartz
The Spring Temple Buddha rises 420 feet, or 128 meters, over Lushan County in China, making it the second-tallest statue in the world.
The Chinese figure held the global height record for more than a decade, a run that began before 2008. India's Statue of Unity ended the reign in 2018 and shifted the title to a new country.
A difference of 177 feet, or 54 meters, now separates the two monuments. The Buddha would have to grow by about 42% to recover the crown. The margin exceeds the full height of three entries on the list: Christ the King, Buddha Dordenma, and Christ the Redeemer.
Only two statues in the roundup clear 400 feet, the Statue of Unity and the Spring Temple Buddha itself. Ushiku Daibutsu in Japan comes closest to joining them at 394 feet, 26 feet short of the Lushan County figure. Guan Yin of the South Sea of Sanya, the next-tallest Chinese work, stands at 354 feet, 66 feet below the Spring Temple Buddha.
The two gaps point in opposite directions. The Buddha's edge over Japan's tallest statue amounts to a small fraction of its deficit to the Statue of Unity. By height, the Lushan County Buddha sits far closer to the pack below it than to the champion above it. Among the 14 statues trailing the Statue of Unity, only the Spring Temple Buddha comes within 200 feet of it.
The Spring Temple Buddha also stands as the tallest religious figure in the roundup. The Statue of Unity commemorates a political leader. Among monuments to faith, the Lushan County Buddha still holds the height advantage on this list. Losing the overall title in 2018 left its standing among sacred works untouched.

# The tallest statues in the world
## Laykyun Sekkya Buddha towers over Muang Monastery
Illustration: Quartz
The Laykyun Sekkya Buddha rises 380 feet, or 116 meters, in Monywa, Myanmar, and dwarfs the Muang Monastery below it. The figure portrays the Buddha.
The Myanmar Buddha trails China's Spring Temple Buddha by 40 feet and India's Statue of Unity by 217 feet. It reaches more than three times the height of Rio de Janeiro's Christ the Redeemer. Set against those benchmarks, the Monywa sculpture belongs with the giants at the head of the list. Its deficit against the Spring Temple Buddha amounts to a small slice of its lead over the Brazilian landmark.
Smaller monuments ring the central statue across the grounds. The ring of lesser structures centers the whole site on a single dominant presence. Every one of them sits in the shadow of the main work and underlines its bulk.
A viewing gallery lets visitors approach for a closer look at the Buddha. The gallery gives the statue a second audience, people who study its details in person alongside those who take it in as a silhouette above the monastery. Each feature the list records at Monywa serves the central Buddha, either by framing it from the ground or by drawing viewers toward it.

# The tallest statues in the world
## Ushiku Daibutsu houses a hall on Buddhism
Illustration: Quartz
The Ushiku Daibutsu in Ibaraki, Japan, rises 394 feet, or 120 meters, and visitors can walk through rooms inside its body. The statue also goes by the Great Buddha of Ushiku, and the list casts it as a forceful symbol of Japanese culture.
An exhibition hall within the figure teaches guests about Buddhism. The monument doubles as a classroom, and a trip there means studying the faith from inside the Buddha's own likeness.
An observation deck on the top floor opens wide views across the surrounding area. A visitor who moves up from the hall below ends at the sculpture's summit and surveys the landscape from it. The layout makes the Daibutsu a building as well as an artwork, and its height becomes a vantage point that sightseers can occupy.
Its 394 feet put the Great Buddha of Ushiku 14 feet above Myanmar's 380-foot Laykyun Sekkya Buddha. China's Spring Temple Buddha exceeds it by 26 feet, and India's Statue of Unity climbs 203 feet higher. The gap to the Chinese Buddha comes to about one-eighth of the gap to the Indian colossus. The 203-foot shortfall alone surpasses the full stature of several entries, among them Poland's Christ the King and Brazil's Christ the Redeemer.
The Ibaraki Buddha also outstrips its two compatriots in the roundup. It clears Sendai Daikannon's 328 feet by 66 feet and the 289-foot Dai Kannon of Kita no Miyako Park by 105 feet. Its margin over Dai Kannon spans several times the distance separating it from the Spring Temple Buddha. Measured in feet, Japan's largest representative has more in common with the Lushan County giant than with either domestic counterpart.

# The tallest statues in the world
## Guan Yin of the South Sea of Sanya sits near the ocean
Illustration: Quartz
Guan Yin of the South Sea of Sanya reaches 354 feet, or 108 meters, and occupies a spot beside the ocean in Hainan, China. Its coastal position sets it apart from the other Chinese giants in the roundup, none of which HowStuffWorks places by the sea. The list presents the site as a spiritual destination for travelers who come for the views and for the culture behind the monument. The statue rests on a lotus throne.
A single Chinese entry on the list outstrips this Hainan colossus. The Spring Temple Buddha in Lushan County exceeds it by 66 feet. The Henan monument to Emperors Yan and Huang trails it by six feet, close enough that the two read as equals in scale. The Monument to Guan Yu in Jingzhou falls 164 feet short of the seaside Guan Yin.
Guan Yin and the Henan pair match in size but not in purpose. The seaside figure draws visitors as a place of faith and scenery. Its closest Chinese rival in stature stands for unity and prosperity. On this list, China's builders reached matching proportions for religious devotion and for a message of collective well-being.
China's entries spread across 230 feet of height, and Guan Yin belongs with the three that crowd the upper end of that span, leaving Jingzhou's general alone at the bottom.

# The tallest statues in the world
## Emperors Yan and Huang symbolize unity and prosperity
Illustration: Quartz
Builders in Henan, China, raised the 348-foot Emperors Yan and Huang to stand for unity and prosperity. Its name invokes two rulers at once, and no other entry on the list refers to a pair of people.
Unity and prosperity describe goals a whole society pursues together. Pairing two emperors in one monument turns the first of those goals into something a visitor can see.
Henan's giant differs in purpose from China's other entries. The Spring Temple Buddha and Guan Yin of the South Sea of Sanya fill spiritual roles, and the Monument to Guan Yu portrays a legendary general. Emperors Yan and Huang alone among them speaks to civic ideals.
At 106 meters, the monument belongs to a group of seven entries that reach 100 meters or more. Guan Yin of the South Sea of Sanya, its predecessor on the list, outstrips it by six feet. Sendai Daikannon, the next entry, falls 20 feet short.
The Statue of Unity clears the Henan pair by 249 feet. Even so, Emperors Yan and Huang reaches more than half that statue's elevation and climbs more than two and a half times higher than Christ the Redeemer.
Two of the seven giants above 100 meters, this one and the Statue of Unity, tie themselves to unity by purpose or by name. Civic ideals, the figures suggest, can command the same scale as faith.

# The tallest statues in the world
## Sendai Daikannon contains a spiral staircase
Illustration: Quartz
Sendai Daikannon reaches 328 feet, or 100 meters, in the Japanese city of Sendai, and guests can explore what lies inside it. A spiral staircase coils up through the statue, and platforms along the way give climbers places to pause and look out.
The staircase turns the statue's size into something a visitor measures with legs. Someone at the base sees a 100-meter form from below. A climber inside covers the same vertical span on foot, one turn of the spiral at a time, and each platform opens an outward vista.
The interior changes what kind of object the monument is. A sealed sculpture offers nothing but an exterior to admire. Sendai Daikannon works more as a tower, with an inner route and stopping points that reward the effort of going up.
Sendai Daikannon falls between Japan's two other entries on the list in stature. Ushiku Daibutsu in Ibaraki stands 66 feet taller at 394 feet. Dai Kannon of Kita no Miyako Park in Hokkaido comes in 39 feet lower at 289 feet. The Statue of Unity in Gujarat, India, exceeds the Sendai monument by 269 feet.
Ushiku Daibutsu opens its interior to visitors as well. At least two of Japan's three statues on the list let people step inside a colossus and gaze out from above. Among the country's entries, size and access go together. The two tallest Japanese statues on the list both invite visitors inside.

# The tallest statues in the world
## Great Buddha of Thailand rises 302 feet in Ang Thong
Illustration: Quartz
The Great Buddha of Thailand climbs 302 feet, or 92 meters, above Ang Thong Province. Its height reaches a little more than half that of the Statue of Unity, the tallest figure in the roundup. It also stands more than twice as tall as Christ the Redeemer in Rio de Janeiro.
Wat Muang in Ang Thong holds a golden seated Buddha known as Luang Phor Yai. A person standing at its fingertips appears tiny beside the figure. A single hand of the statue, by that measure, outsizes the people who come to see it.

# The tallest statues in the world
## Motherland Calls commemorates the Battle of Stalingrad
Illustration: Quartz
Motherland Calls rises 279 feet, or 85 meters, above Volgograd, Russia, as a memorial to the Battle of Stalingrad during World War II. Its subject sets it apart from its neighbors in the roundup. Buddhas, depictions of Christ, and the Virgin Mary account for eight of the 15 entries. Other entries portray historical or legendary people, from a political leader such as Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel to a general such as Guan Yu. Motherland Calls alone commemorates a battle, and its subject belongs to a whole population.
A sword held high defines the pose. HowStuffWorks describes the statue as dynamic, and the raised blade lends the sculpture a sense of motion. The faith-based entries convey other qualities. Dai Kannon of Kita no Miyako Park in Hokkaido, for one, represents compassion and mercy. Motion and mercy make an unlikely pair on one list, and the contrast shows the range of purposes behind these giants.
The publication reads the upraised weapon as a representation of resilience. Its interpretation ties the statue's form to its purpose. A wartime memorial built around a blade and an energetic stance speaks to endurance through conflict more than to quiet mourning. The statue's name reinforces that reading, casting the homeland as a voice summoning its people.
HowStuffWorks mentions a weapon on one other entry. The Monument to Guan Yu in Jingzhou, China, shows the general's weapon and robe in intricate detail. The Jingzhou statue stands 89 feet shorter than Motherland Calls. The two works arm their subjects for different ends. Guan Yu embodies one man's strength and loyalty, while the Volgograd memorial honors a collective wartime ordeal.
Motherland Calls falls 318 feet short of the Statue of Unity in Gujarat, India. It stands more than twice as tall as Christ the Redeemer in Rio de Janeiro. Its inclusion shows that national memory can hold its own among devotional colossi, and that a statue can earn a spot through what it recalls as much as through its size.

# The tallest statues in the world
## Virgin Mary statue crowns a Batangas pilgrimage center
Illustration: Quartz
The Virgin Mary statue at Montemaria stands 315 feet, or 96 meters, tall atop the Montemaria International Pilgrimage Center in Batangas City, Philippines. Its perch above the center commands a view of the surrounding coastline. Mounting the figure on the center itself fuses the monument and the destination into one site. The statue bears the name Mother of All Asia Tower of Peace and forms the centerpiece of a pilgrimage complex at the far southern end of Batangas Bay.
Pilgrims sit at the heart of the statue's purpose. HowStuffWorks describes the figure as a source of hope for the faithful who travel to Batangas. The image casts the statue as a fixed point that guides each journey. Its dedication extends to a public cause, harmony and peace among the nations and people of the region around it. The phrase Tower of Peace echoes that pledge and turns a devotional image into a regional appeal. The grounds have drawn both devotees and tourists. Sightseers who come for the spectacle encounter a message of peace aimed past the circle of believers. Their visits widen the statue's audience beyond the worshippers it serves.
The Batangas statue exceeds both depictions of Christ on the list by a wide margin. Christ the King in Swiebodzin, Poland, falls 143 feet short of the Montemaria figure. Christ the Redeemer in Rio de Janeiro trails the Batangas statue by 190 feet. The Virgin Mary reaches more than two and a half times the Rio figure's height. The 190-foot gap exceeds the entire height of three statues on the list: Christ the King, Buddha Dordenma, and Christ the Redeemer. The Montemaria figure is the list's only portrayal of Mary. The height gaps hand the title of largest Christian monument among the 15 entries to Batangas City, ahead of the two Christ figures in Poland and Brazil.

# The tallest statues in the world
## Christ the King wears a crown of sovereignty
Illustration: Quartz
Christ the King stands 172 feet, or 52.5 meters, tall in Swiebodzin, Poland, and the list credits it as the world's tallest depiction of Jesus. The monument draws frequent comparisons with Christ the Redeemer in Rio de Janeiro, and it outstrips that Brazilian figure by 47 feet.
The statue pays tribute to Pope John Paul II and to the Catholic faith as a whole. The dedication salutes a single churchman and an entire creed in the same gesture. HowStuffWorks stresses that the work holds deep importance for the Polish people. Its meaning reaches past religion and into the life of the country.
A crown on the colossus's head signals Christ's sovereignty. The headpiece lays a message of rule over the message of devotion, and it echoes the title the statue bears. Name and ornament state one idea twice, once in words and once in form. A visitor unaware of the papal dedication can read kingship in the silhouette.
Each of the 10 entries numbered ahead of Christ the King surpasses it in stature, and none of them portrays Jesus. Dai Kannon of Kita no Miyako Park and the Monument to Guan Yu, which follow it in the numbering, top it as well. Size by itself would earn the Swiebodzin landmark little notice in this company. Its distinction rests on supremacy within one subject, a narrower claim than the outright prize the Statue of Unity holds.
The record covers images of Jesus alone. The loftiest Christian figure in the roundup stands in Batangas City, Philippines, where the Virgin Mary statue exceeds Christ the King by 143 feet. Christian imagery on the list spans the Philippines, Poland, and Brazil, while Buddhas fill many of the other slots. Christ the King owes its standing to a narrow category. Its honor depends on what it depicts as much as on how high it climbs.

# The tallest statues in the world
## Dai Kannon of Kita no Miyako Park represents mercy
Illustration: Quartz
Dai Kannon of Kita no Miyako Park reaches 289 feet, or 88 meters, above Hokkaido, Japan, and HowStuffWorks reports that it once held the record as the tallest statue in the world. Builders completed the figure in 1989. The list gives no date for when the title passed to another monument. The length of its reign goes unstated.
Compassion and mercy define the message the monument carries, according to HowStuffWorks. Its theme separates it from entries that honor a statesman or commemorate a battle. In Hokkaido, colossal scale serves a personal virtue. A sculpture of record-setting size devoted to a quality people extend to one another puts gentleness at the center of its purpose.
Quiet parkland frames the figure. Miyako Park surrounds its base, and the source calls the grounds tranquil. HowStuffWorks also counts the statue among Japan's best-known landmarks. # The tallest statues in the world
From India's 597-foot Statue of Unity to Bhutan's Buddha Dordenma, 15 colossal figures honor heroes, faiths, and national identity.
1 / 17
List slides
The tallest statues in the world
List slides Previous Start over
ByCris Tolomia
·Updated November 3, 2026
Add QZ to Google
Illustration: Quartz
Stand at the base of a colossus, and its size registers in your neck before it registers in your head. The face hovers above the rooftops, and the people milling around its feet look like toys. Societies have raised enormous figures for centuries to declare ambition in a form no one can miss. Each one asks a passerby to look up, and each one prompts a question about the people who built it. What did those builders value enough to cast at this scale? Culture, faith, and collective self-image supply most of the answers, and the biggest of these works turn those abstractions into objects you can walk around.
Height alone gives a misleading picture of these giants. A tape measure can settle which one wins the contest, but it cannot explain what moved anyone to erect it. Some pay tribute to a historical leader. Others embody spiritual devotion. A third group carries a message about unity or national identity, a public argument about who a populace believes it is. Proportion poses its own trap. A photo of a single sculpture against open sky can make a modest piece and a towering one look alike. Nearby pedestrians or buildings give the eye something to compare against, and without those reference points the raw numbers lose their meaning.
HowStuffWorks gathered 15 of the world's tallest statues in a December 2024 list by writer Mack Hayden. The roundup spans 10 countries. China supplies four entries and Japan three, and India, Myanmar, Thailand, Russia, the Philippines, Poland, Brazil, and Bhutan contribute one apiece. Each entry pairs a location with feet-and-meters dimensions, plus a brief sketch of what the statue stands for. The publication does not explain how it arrived at those dimensions. Its numbering departs from a clean tallest-to-shortest sequence in several places. The slides that follow keep the publication's order and make no claim about which entry outranks its neighbor in stature. Hayden presents the monuments both as landmarks and as doorways into history and into the ways communities have celebrated their heroes and ideals.
texts.3:
# The tallest statues in the world
## Statue of Unity honors Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
Illustration: Quartz
The Statue of Unity in Gujarat, India, stands 597 feet, or 182 meters, tall. No other figure on the list reaches that elevation, and HowStuffWorks calls it the reigning champion among the world's tallest statues.
A statesman inspired the giant. The monument honors Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, who served as India's first deputy prime minister. Its subject sets it apart from most of the company it keeps. Eleven of the 15 entries carry the name of a Buddha, Guan Yin, Kannon, the Virgin Mary, or Christ. The Gujarat monument belongs to a smaller group of four that honors a statesman, a pair of emperors, a legendary general, and a wartime battle.
Patel's likeness outstrips the rest of that group by a wide margin. Emperors Yan and Huang, the tallest of the other three, falls 249 feet short of the Indian figure. The shortfall exceeds the full height of four entries on the list, among them Christ the King and Buddha Dordenma.
Patel's office marks a difference in kind as well. The other three nonreligious entries draw on rulers, legend, and a World War II battle. The Gujarat colossus celebrates a man who held a post in India's own government, a leader from the country's modern political life.
The monument's name points the same direction. Its title holds up unity, a civic ideal, and attaching that word to the tallest entry places a national value at the summit of a list crowded with holy figures.
The Statue of Liberty supplies a familiar yardstick. The Gujarat giant climbs to more than twice the American landmark's stature. Rio de Janeiro's Christ the Redeemer offers a second measure, and the Indian statue rises close to five times as high. Both comparisons turn an abstract number into something a reader can picture.
On the list's own figures, no religious statue matches the scale of this tribute to a political leader.
texts.4:
# The tallest statues in the world
## Spring Temple Buddha reigned for more than a decade
Illustration: Quartz
The Spring Temple Buddha rises 420 feet, or 128 meters, over Lushan County in China, making it the second-tallest statue in the world.
The Chinese figure held the global height record for more than a decade, a run that began before 2008. India's Statue of Unity ended the reign in 2018 and shifted the title to a new country.
A difference of 177 feet, or 54 meters, now separates the two monuments. The Buddha would have to grow by about 42% to recover the crown. The margin exceeds the full height of three entries on the list: Christ the King, Buddha Dordenma, and Christ the Redeemer.
Only two statues in the roundup clear 400 feet, the Statue of Unity and the Spring Temple Buddha itself. Ushiku Daibutsu in Japan comes closest to joining them at 394 feet, 26 feet short of the Lushan County figure. Guan Yin of the South Sea of Sanya, the next-tallest Chinese work, stands at 354 feet, 66 feet below the Spring Temple Buddha.
The two gaps point in opposite directions. The Buddha's edge over Japan's tallest statue amounts to a small fraction of its deficit to the Statue of Unity. By height, the Lushan County Buddha sits far closer to the pack below it than to the champion above it. Among the 14 statues trailing the Statue of Unity, only the Spring Temple Buddha comes within 200 feet of it.
The Spring Temple Buddha also stands as the tallest religious figure in the roundup. The Statue of Unity commemorates a political leader. Among monuments to faith, the Lushan County Buddha still holds the height advantage on this list. Losing the overall title in 2018 left its standing among sacred works untouched.
texts.5:
# The tallest statues in the world
## Laykyun Sekkya Buddha towers over Muang Monastery
Illustration: Quartz
The Laykyun Sekkya Buddha rises 380 feet, or 116 meters, in Monywa, Myanmar, and dwarfs the Muang Monastery below it. The figure portrays the Buddha.
The Myanmar Buddha trails China's Spring Temple Buddha by 40 feet and India's Statue of Unity by 217 feet. It reaches more than three times the height of Rio de Janeiro's Christ the Redeemer. Set against those benchmarks, the Monywa sculpture belongs with the giants at the head of the list. Its deficit against the Spring Temple Buddha amounts to a small slice of its lead over the Brazilian landmark.
Smaller monuments ring the central statue across the grounds. The ring of lesser structures centers the whole site on a single dominant presence. Every one of them sits in the shadow of the main work and underlines its bulk.
A viewing gallery lets visitors approach for a closer look at the Buddha. The gallery gives the statue a second audience, people who study its details in person alongside those who take it in as a silhouette above the monastery. Each feature the list records at Monywa serves the central Buddha, either by framing it from the ground or by drawing viewers toward it.
texts.6:
# The tallest statues in the world
## Ushiku Daibutsu houses a hall on Buddhism
Illustration: Quartz
The Ushiku Daibutsu in Ibaraki, Japan, rises 394 feet, or 120 meters, and visitors can walk through rooms inside its body. The statue also goes by the Great Buddha of Ushiku, and the list casts it as a forceful symbol of Japanese culture.
An exhibition hall within the figure teaches guests about Buddhism. The monument doubles as a classroom, and a trip there means studying the faith from inside the Buddha's own likeness.
An observation deck on the top floor opens wide views across the surrounding area. A visitor who moves up from the hall below ends at the sculpture's summit and surveys the landscape from it. The layout makes the Daibutsu a building as well as an artwork, and its height becomes a vantage point that sightseers can occupy.
Its 394 feet put the Great Buddha of Ushiku 14 feet above Myanmar's 380-foot Laykyun Sekkya Buddha. China's Spring Temple Buddha exceeds it by 26 feet, and India's Statue of Unity climbs 203 feet higher. The gap to the Chinese Buddha comes to about one-eighth of the gap to the Indian colossus. The 203-foot shortfall alone surpasses the full stature of several entries, among them Poland's Christ the King and Brazil's Christ the Redeemer.
The Ibaraki Buddha also outstrips its two compatriots in the roundup. It clears Sendai Daikannon's 328 feet by 66 feet and the 289-foot Dai Kannon of Kita no Miyako Park by 105 feet. Its margin over Dai Kannon spans several times the distance separating it from the Spring Temple Buddha. Measured in feet, Japan's largest representative has more in common with the Lushan County giant than with either domestic counterpart.
texts.7:
# The tallest statues in the world
## Guan Yin of the South Sea of Sanya sits near the ocean
Illustration: Quartz
Guan Yin of the South Sea of Sanya reaches 354 feet, or 108 meters, and occupies a spot beside the ocean in Hainan, China. Its coastal position sets it apart from the other Chinese giants in the roundup, none of which HowStuffWorks places by the sea. The list presents the site as a spiritual destination for travelers who come for the views and for the culture behind the monument. The statue rests on a lotus throne.
A single Chinese entry on the list outstrips this Hainan colossus. The Spring Temple Buddha in Lushan County exceeds it by 66 feet. The Henan monument to Emperors Yan and Huang trails it by six feet, close enough that the two read as equals in scale. The Monument to Guan Yu in Jingzhou falls 164 feet short of the seaside Guan Yin.
Guan Yin and the Henan pair match in size but not in purpose. The seaside figure draws visitors as a place of faith and scenery. Its closest Chinese rival in stature stands for unity and prosperity. On this list, China's builders reached matching proportions for religious devotion and for a message of collective well-being.
China's entries spread across 230 feet of height, and Guan Yin belongs with the three that crowd the upper end of that span, leaving Jingzhou's general alone at the bottom.
texts.8:
# The tallest statues in the world
## Emperors Yan and Huang symbolize unity and prosperity
Illustration: Quartz
Builders in Henan, China, raised the 348-foot Emperors Yan and Huang to stand for unity and prosperity. Its name invokes two rulers at once, and no other entry on the list refers to a pair of people.
Unity and prosperity describe goals a whole society pursues together. Pairing two emperors in one monument turns the first of those goals into something a visitor can see.
Henan's giant differs in purpose from China's other entries. The Spring Temple Buddha and Guan Yin of the South Sea of Sanya fill spiritual roles, and the Monument to Guan Yu portrays a legendary general. Emperors Yan and Huang alone among them speaks to civic ideals.
At 106 meters, the monument belongs to a group of seven entries that reach 100 meters or more. Guan Yin of the South Sea of Sanya, its predecessor on the list, outstrips it by six feet. Sendai Daikannon, the next entry, falls 20 feet short.
The Statue of Unity clears the Henan pair by 249 feet. Even so, Emperors Yan and Huang reaches more than half that statue's elevation and climbs more than two and a half times higher than Christ the Redeemer.
Two of the seven giants above 100 meters, this one and the Statue of Unity, tie themselves to unity by purpose or by name. Civic ideals, the figures suggest, can command the same scale as faith.
texts.9:
# The tallest statues in the world
## Sendai Daikannon contains a spiral staircase
Illustration: Quartz
Sendai Daikannon reaches 328 feet, or 100 meters, in the Japanese city of Sendai, and guests can explore what lies inside it. A spiral staircase coils up through the statue, and platforms along the way give climbers places to pause and look out.
The staircase turns the statue's size into something a visitor measures with legs. Someone at the base sees a 100-meter form from below. A climber inside covers the same vertical span on foot, one turn of the spiral at a time, and each platform opens an outward vista.
The interior changes what kind of object the monument is. A sealed sculpture offers nothing but an exterior to admire. Sendai Daikannon works more as a tower, with an inner route and stopping points that reward the effort of going up.
Sendai Daikannon falls between Japan's two other entries on the list in stature. Ushiku Daibutsu in Ibaraki stands 66 feet taller at 394 feet. Dai Kannon of Kita no Miyako Park in Hokkaido comes in 39 feet lower at 289 feet. The Statue of Unity in Gujarat, India, exceeds the Sendai monument by 269 feet.
Ushiku Daibutsu opens its interior to visitors as well. At least two of Japan's three statues on the list let people step inside a colossus and gaze out from above. Among the country's entries, size and access go together. The two tallest Japanese statues on the list both invite visitors inside.
texts.10:
# The tallest statues in the world
## Great Buddha of Thailand rises 302 feet in Ang Thong
Illustration: Quartz
The Great Buddha of Thailand climbs 302 feet, or 92 meters, above Ang Thong Province. Its height reaches a little more than half that of the Statue of Unity, the tallest figure in the roundup. It also stands more than twice as tall as Christ the Redeemer in Rio de Janeiro.
Wat Muang in Ang Thong holds a golden seated Buddha known as Luang Phor Yai. A person standing at its fingertips appears tiny beside the figure. A single hand of the statue, by that measure, outsizes the people who come to see it.
texts.11:
# The tallest statues in the world
## Motherland Calls commemorates the Battle of Stalingrad
Illustration: Quartz
Motherland Calls rises 279 feet, or 85 meters, above Volgograd, Russia, as a memorial to the Battle of Stalingrad during World War II. Its subject sets it apart from its neighbors in the roundup. Buddhas, depictions of Christ, and the Virgin Mary account for eight of the 15 entries. Other entries portray historical or legendary people, from a political leader such as Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel to a general such as Guan Yu. Motherland Calls alone commemorates a battle, and its subject belongs to a whole population.
A sword held high defines the pose. HowStuffWorks describes the statue as dynamic, and the raised blade lends the sculpture a sense of motion. The faith-based entries convey other qualities. Dai Kannon of Kita no Miyako Park in Hokkaido, for one, represents compassion and mercy. Motion and mercy make an unlikely pair on one list, and the contrast shows the range of purposes behind these giants.
The publication reads the upraised weapon as a representation of resilience. Its interpretation ties the statue's form to its purpose. A wartime memorial built around a blade and an energetic stance speaks to endurance through conflict more than to quiet mourning. The statue's name reinforces that reading, casting the homeland as a voice summoning its people.
HowStuffWorks mentions a weapon on one other entry. The Monument to Guan Yu in Jingzhou, China, shows the general's weapon and robe in intricate detail. The Jingzhou statue stands 89 feet shorter than Motherland Calls. The two works arm their subjects for different ends. Guan Yu embodies one man's strength and loyalty, while the Volgograd memorial honors a collective wartime ordeal.
Motherland Calls falls 318 feet short of the Statue of Unity in Gujarat, India. It stands more than twice as tall as Christ the Redeemer in Rio de Janeiro. Its inclusion shows that national memory can hold its own among devotional colossi, and that a statue can earn a spot through what it recalls as much as through its size.

# The tallest statues in the world
## Virgin Mary statue crowns a Batangas pilgrimage center
Illustration: Quartz
The Virgin Mary statue at Montemaria stands 315 feet, or 96 meters, tall atop the Montemaria International Pilgrimage Center in Batangas City, Philippines. Its perch above the center commands a view of the surrounding coastline. Mounting the figure on the center itself fuses the monument and the destination into one site. The statue bears the name Mother of All Asia Tower of Peace and forms the centerpiece of a pilgrimage complex at the far southern end of Batangas Bay.
Pilgrims sit at the heart of the statue's purpose. HowStuffWorks describes the figure as a source of hope for the faithful who travel to Batangas. The image casts the statue as a fixed point that guides each journey. Its dedication extends to a public cause, harmony and peace among the nations and people of the region around it. The phrase Tower of Peace echoes that pledge and turns a devotional image into a regional appeal. The grounds have drawn both devotees and tourists. Sightseers who come for the spectacle encounter a message of peace aimed past the circle of believers. Their visits widen the statue's audience beyond the worshippers it serves.
The Batangas statue exceeds both depictions of Christ on the list by a wide margin. Christ the King in Swiebodzin, Poland, falls 143 feet short of the Montemaria figure. Christ the Redeemer in Rio de Janeiro trails the Batangas statue by 190 feet. The Virgin Mary reaches more than two and a half times the Rio figure's height. The 190-foot gap exceeds the entire height of three statues on the list: Christ the King, Buddha Dordenma, and Christ the Redeemer. The Montemaria figure is the list's only portrayal of Mary. The height gaps hand the title of largest Christian monument among the 15 entries to Batangas City, ahead of the two Christ figures in Poland and Brazil.

# The tallest statues in the world
## Christ the King wears a crown of sovereignty
Illustration: Quartz
Christ the King stands 172 feet, or 52.5 meters, tall in Swiebodzin, Poland, and the list credits it as the world's tallest depiction of Jesus. The monument draws frequent comparisons with Christ the Redeemer in Rio de Janeiro, and it outstrips that Brazilian figure by 47 feet.
The statue pays tribute to Pope John Paul II and to the Catholic faith as a whole. The dedication salutes a single churchman and an entire creed in the same gesture. HowStuffWorks stresses that the work holds deep importance for the Polish people. Its meaning reaches past religion and into the life of the country.

Name and ornament state one idea twice, once in words and once in form. A visitor unaware of the papal dedication can read kingship in the silhouette.

Its distinction rests on supremacy within one subject, a narrower claim than the outright prize the Statue of Unity holds.
The record covers images of Jesus alone. The loftiest Christian figure in the roundup stands in Batangas City, Philippines, where the Virgin Mary statue exceeds Christ the King by 143 feet. Christian imagery on the list spans the Philippines, Poland, and Brazil, while Buddhas fill many of the other slots. Christ the King owes its standing to a narrow category. Its honor depends on what it depicts as much as on how high it climbs.

## Dai Kannon of Kita no Miyako Park represents mercy
Illustration: Quartz
Dai Kannon of Kita no Miyako Park reaches 289 feet, or 88 meters, above Hokkaido, Japan, and HowStuffWorks reports that it once held the record as the tallest statue in the world. Illustration: Quartz
Stand at the base of a colossus, and its size registers in your neck before it registers in your head. The face hovers above the rooftops, and the people milling around its feet look like toys. Societies have raised enormous figures for centuries to declare ambition in a form no one can miss. Each one asks a passerby to look up, and each one prompts a question about the people who built it. What did those builders value enough to cast at this scale? Culture, faith, and collective self-image supply most of the answers, and the biggest of these works turn those abstractions into objects you can walk around.
Height alone gives a misleading picture of these giants. A tape measure can settle which one wins the contest, but it cannot explain what moved anyone to erect it. Some pay tribute to a historical leader. Others embody spiritual devotion. A third group carries a message about unity or national identity, a public argument about who a populace believes it is. Proportion poses its own trap. A photo of a single sculpture against open sky can make a modest piece and a towering one look alike. Nearby pedestrians or buildings give the eye something to compare against, and without those reference points the raw numbers lose their meaning.
HowStuffWorks gathered 15 of the world's tallest statues in a December 2024 list by writer Mack Hayden. The roundup spans 10 countries. China supplies four entries and Japan three, and India, Myanmar, Thailand, Russia, the Philippines, Poland, Brazil, and Bhutan contribute one apiece. Each entry pairs a location with feet-and-meters dimensions, plus a brief sketch of what the statue stands for. The publication does not explain how it arrived at those dimensions. Its numbering departs from a clean tallest-to-shortest sequence in several places. The slides that follow keep the publication's order and make no claim about which entry outranks its neighbor in stature. Hayden presents the monuments both as landmarks and as doorways into history and into the ways communities have celebrated their heroes and ideals.

# The tallest statues in the world
## Statue of Unity honors Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
Illustration: Quartz
The Statue of Unity in Gujarat, India, stands 597 feet, or 182 meters, tall. No other figure on the list reaches that elevation, and HowStuffWorks calls it the reigning champion among the world's tallest statues.
A statesman inspired the giant. The monument honors Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, who served as India's first deputy prime minister. Its subject sets it apart from most of the company it keeps. Eleven of the 15 entries carry the name of a Buddha, Guan Yin, Kannon, the Virgin Mary, or Christ. The Gujarat monument belongs to a smaller group of four that honors a statesman, a pair of emperors, a legendary general, and a wartime battle.
Patel's likeness outstrips the rest of that group by a wide margin. Emperors Yan and Huang, the tallest of the other three, falls 249 feet short of the Indian figure. The shortfall exceeds the full height of four entries on the list, among them Christ the King and Buddha Dordenma.
Patel's office marks a difference in kind as well. The other three nonreligious entries draw on rulers, legend, and a World War II battle. The Gujarat colossus celebrates a man who held a post in India's own government, a leader from the country's modern political life.
The monument's name points the same direction. Its title holds up unity, a civic ideal, and attaching that word to the tallest entry places a national value at the summit of a list crowded with holy figures.
The Statue of Liberty supplies a familiar yardstick. The Gujarat giant climbs to more than twice the American landmark's stature. Rio de Janeiro's Christ the Redeemer offers a second measure, and the Indian statue rises close to five times as high. Both comparisons turn an abstract number into something a reader can picture.
On the list's own figures, no religious statue matches the scale of this tribute to a political leader.

# The tallest statues in the world
## Spring Temple Buddha reigned for more than a decade
Illustration: Quartz
The Spring Temple Buddha rises 420 feet, or 128 meters, over Lushan County in China, making it the second-tallest statue in the world.
The Chinese figure held the global height record for more than a decade, a run that began before 2008. India's Statue of Unity ended the reign in 2018 and shifted the title to a new country.
A difference of 177 feet, or 54 meters, now separates the two monuments. The Buddha would have to grow by about 42% to recover the crown. The margin exceeds the full height of three entries on the list: Christ the King, Buddha Dordenma, and Christ the Redeemer.
Only two statues in the roundup clear 400 feet, the Statue of Unity and the Spring Temple Buddha itself. Ushiku Daibutsu in Japan comes closest to joining them at 394 feet, 26 feet short of the Lushan County figure. Guan Yin of the South Sea of Sanya, the next-tallest Chinese work, stands at 354 feet, 66 feet below the Spring Temple Buddha.
The two gaps point in opposite directions. The Buddha's edge over Japan's tallest statue amounts to a small fraction of its deficit to the Statue of Unity. By height, the Lushan County Buddha sits far closer to the pack below it than to the champion above it. Among the 14 statues trailing the Statue of Unity, only the Spring Temple Buddha comes within 200 feet of it.
The Spring Temple Buddha also stands as the tallest religious figure in the roundup. The Statue of Unity commemorates a political leader. Among monuments to faith, the Lushan County Buddha still holds the height advantage on this list. Losing the overall title in 2018 left its standing among sacred works untouched.

The Myanmar Buddha trails China's Spring Temple Buddha by 40 feet and India's Statue of Unity by 217 feet. It reaches more than three times the height of Rio de Janeiro's Christ the Redeemer. Set against those benchmarks, the Monywa sculpture belongs with the giants at the head of the list. Its deficit against the Spring Temple Buddha amounts to a small slice of its lead over the Brazilian landmark.
Smaller monuments ring the central statue across the grounds. The ring of lesser structures centers the whole site on a single dominant presence. Every one of them sits in the shadow of the main work and underlines its bulk.
A viewing gallery lets visitors approach for a closer look at the Buddha. The gallery gives the statue a second audience, people who study its details in person alongside those who take it in as a silhouette above the monastery. Each feature the list records at Monywa serves the central Buddha, either by framing it from the ground or by drawing viewers toward it.

## Ushiku Daibutsu houses a hall on Buddhism
Illustration: Quartz
The Ushiku Daibutsu in Ibaraki, Japan, rises 394 feet, or 120 meters, and visitors can walk through rooms inside its body. The statue also goes by the Great Buddha of Ushiku, and the list casts it as a forceful symbol of Japanese culture.
An exhibition hall within the figure teaches guests about Buddhism. The monument doubles as a classroom, and a trip there means studying the faith from inside the Buddha's own likeness.
An observation deck on the top floor opens wide views across the surrounding area. A visitor who moves up from the hall below ends at the sculpture's summit and surveys the landscape from it. The layout makes the Daibutsu a building as well as an artwork, and its height becomes a vantage point that sightseers can occupy.
Its 394 feet put the Great Buddha of Ushiku 14 feet above Myanmar's 380-foot Laykyun Sekkya Buddha. China's Spring Temple Buddha exceeds it by 26 feet, and India's Statue of Unity climbs 203 feet higher. The gap to the Chinese Buddha comes to about one-eighth of the gap to the Indian colossus. Illustration: Quartz
Guan Yin of the South Sea of Sanya reaches 354 feet, or 108 meters, and occupies a spot beside the ocean in Hainan, China. ## Emperors Yan and Huang symbolize unity and prosperity
Illustration: Quartz
Builders in Henan, China, raised the 348-foot Emperors Yan and Huang to stand for unity and prosperity. Its name invokes two rulers at once, and no other entry on the list refers to a pair of people.
Unity and prosperity describe goals a whole society pursues together. Pairing two emperors in one monument turns the first of those goals into something a visitor can see.

Illustration: Quartz

## Motherland Calls commemorates the Battle of Stalingrad
Illustration: Quartz
Motherland Calls rises 279 feet, or 85 meters, above Volgograd, Russia, as a memorial to the Battle of Stalingrad during World War II. Its subject sets it apart from its neighbors in the roundup. Buddhas, depictions of Christ, and the Virgin Mary account for eight of the 15 entries.
